subject: Nanotechnology
title: How Photolithography Works
description: A quick, practical guide to How Photolithography Works.

hook.text: Every chip in every phone was printed with light — photolithography is the backbone of modern tech.

buildup.text: A light-sensitive coating called photoresist is spread on a silicon wafer in a thin, even layer.

discovery.text: Ultraviolet light shines through a mask, transferring a circuit pattern onto the resist below.

twist.text: Where light hits, the resist changes — exposed areas dissolve away, leaving the pattern behind.

climax.text: This process repeats dozens of times to build a chip layer by layer — each aligned to nanometer precision.

punchline.text: Printing with light — one layer at a time — built the digital age.

quiz.question: What is the role of photoresist in lithography?
options: It conducts electricity through the circuit
It changes when exposed to light, enabling pattern transfer
It cools the silicon wafer during processing
